newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen stable as Chinese demand eases.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen stable as Chinese demand eases.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were seen steady with activites slugglish on typical quiet Monday as Chinese demand softens, traders said.
High sulphur 180-cst fuel oil levels were assessed at $123/$125 per tonne on Friday.
January swaps were quoted Monday at a steady but wider $120.50/$122.00 against Friday's $121/$121.50.
The market direction remained vague as most traders had just returned to their desk, having recovered from the festive holiday mood after the New Year holiday break, a trader said.
"We are still assessing demand and supply," said another trader.

Traders said two cargoes of 30,000 tonne each of 180-cst fuel oil for late January arrivial to China from South Korea were traded at $8.80 per tonne over Singapore spot quotes, on a cost-anf-freight basis.
A trader said the deals were probably done in December when Chinese demand were firm.
But current premia to China were indicated at $8.00 per tonne to southern China for February delivery cargoes. Freight costs from South Korea to China were assessed at $7 per tonne.
Chinese demand had subsided after a period of heavy buying seen late last month, said traders
They said February supplies from the Mideast and South Korea remained constant.
